arabic_blocks: [960] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر عن عباد بن تميم عن عمه قال خرج النبي ﷺ يستسقي وحول رداءه
english_blocks: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from his uncle, who said:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to seek rain and turned his cloak.

notes: Retains the full chain and the selected Abbad spelling. Turning the cloak is not expanded to inside out, a direction or an extra putting-on action.

arabic_blocks: [961] حدثنا قتيبة حدثنا مغيرة بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا رفع رأسه من الركعة الآخرة يقول اللهم أنج عياش بن أبي ربيعة اللهم أنج سلمة بن هشام اللهم أنج الوليد بن الوليد اللهم أنج المستضعفين من المؤمنين اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر اللهم اجعلها سنين كسني يوسف وأن النبي ﷺ قال: غفار غفر الله لها وأسلم سالمها الله قال ابن أبي الزناد عن أبيه هذا كله في الصبح
english_blocks: Qutaybah related to us. Mughirah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his head in the last unit of prayer, he would say, “O Allah, rescue ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah. O Allah, rescue Salamah ibn Hisham. O Allah, rescue al-Walid ibn al-Walid. O Allah, rescue the oppressed believers. O Allah, intensify Your pressure upon Mudar. O Allah, make it years like the years of Yusuf.” And the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Ghifar—may Allah forgive it; and Aslam—may Allah grant it peace.”
Ibn Abi al-Zinad said, from his father: All of this was in the morning prayer.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The complete repeated invocations, both tribal names and both Prophet honorifics are retained. The morning-prayer comment remains separately attributed to Ibn Abi al-Zinad from his father.
The source names Mughirah ibn Abd al-Rahman, as does the modern print; Brill reads Ubayd al-Rahman. The selected wording is unchanged.
The Ghifar and Aslam formulas are rendered as invocations, as in the Khan comparison; no tribe explanation or legal ruling is inserted.
Modern printed reference 1006. Both Arabic print locations and the English comparison bodies were individually matched. This is new AI-assisted English, not Darussalam wording.
review.reviewScope: AI-assisted full-span working translation of the unchanged selected Arabic, checked against the located English bodies and visually inspected Arabic print pages. Independent Arabic, English, context, reference and spoken-word review remains pending.

arabic_blocks: [962] حدثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق قال كنا عند عبد الله، فقال إن النبي ﷺ لما رأى من الناس إدبارا قال اللهم سبع كسبع يوسف فأخذتهم سنة حصت كل شيء حتى أكلوا الجلود والميتة والجيف وينظر أحدهم إلى السماء فيرى الدخان من الجوع فأتاه أبو سفيان، فقال: يا محمد إنك تأمر بطاعة الله وبصلة الرحم وإن قومك قد هلكوا فادع الله لهم قال الله تعالى { فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين } إلى قوله { عائدون يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى } فالبطشة يوم بدر وقد مضت الدخان والبطشة واللزام وآية الروم
english_blocks: ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said:

We were with ‘Abdullah, and he said: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw the people turning away, he said, “O Allah, seven like the seven of Yusuf.” A year of scarcity overtook them and consumed everything, until they ate hides, carrion and decaying carcasses. One of them would look at the sky and see smoke from hunger. Abu Sufyan came to him and said, “O Muhammad, you command obedience to Allah and maintaining ties of kinship. Your people have perished, so supplicate to Allah for them.” Allah Most High said, “So watch for the day when the sky brings clear smoke,” up to His words, “returning—the day We strike the greatest blow.” The blow was on the day of Badr. The smoke, the blow, al-lizam and the sign of the Romans have already passed.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The chosen digital Quranic excerpt is abbreviated. Its opening, up-to-His-words bridge and fragment beginning returning remain; missing words such as innakum are not silently supplied from the prints. This is not a standalone complete Quran translation.

The source supplies seven without a noun; the working English preserves that ellipsis. A year of scarcity renders sanah, without a claim that the total duration was exactly one year. The people are not expanded into a named tribe or a refusal of Islam.
Al-lizam remains a transliterated source term rather than replacing it with an inferred event; the final list contains four named items. No missing moon item is borrowed from parallel reports.

arabic_blocks: [963] حدثنا عمرو بن علي قال: حدثنا أبو قتيبة قال: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن دينار عن أبيه قال: سمعت ابن عمر يتمثل بشعر أبي طالب
وأبيض يستسقي الغمام بوجهه
ثمال اليتامى عصمة للأرامل
وقال عمر بن حمزة حدثنا سالم عن أبيه ربما ذكرت قول الشاعر وأنا أنظر إلى وجه النبي ﷺ يستسقي فما ينزل حتى يجيش كل ميزاب
وأبيض يستسقي الغمام بوجهه
ثمال اليتامى عصمة للأرامل
وهو قول أبي طالب
english_blocks: ‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: Abu Qutaybah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar related to us, from his father, who said:
I heard Ibn ‘Umar reciting Abu Talib’s poetry:
And a fair one, through whose face rain is sought from the clouds,
a refuge for orphans, a protection for widows.
And ‘Umar ibn Hamzah said: Salim related to us, from his father:
At times I remembered the poet’s words while looking at the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as he sought rain. He would not come down until every waterspout gushed:
And a fair one, through whose face rain is sought from the clouds,
a refuge for orphans, a protection for widows.
And these are Abu Talib’s words.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Both poetry occurrences, both chain portions and the final attribution are retained in source order. Modern printed references 1008 and 1009 are already both present within selected 963; no extra app number is invented.

Bewley renders abyad as faultless and Khan as white, with an explanatory Prophet identification. Fair one is a provisional lexical rendering that does not add that identification. Through whose face and the clouds remain explicit; neither is paraphrased as a request to pray.

Ibn Hajar explains thimal with meanings including support and refuge, and ismah as protection from harm. Refuge and protection are provisional lexical choices here. No historical or legal commentary is added to the narration.

The source says he would not come down; the draft does not insert from the pulpit. The narrator genealogy remains Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Dinar from his father, despite the shortened English introductions.
Modern printed reference 1008, 1009. Both Arabic print locations and the English comparison bodies were individually matched. This is new AI-assisted English, not Darussalam wording.

arabic_blocks: [964] حدثنا الحسن بن محمد قال: حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله الأنصارى قال: حدثني أبي عبد الله ابن المثنى عن ثمامة بن عبد الله بن أنس عن أنس أن عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه كان إذا قحطوا استسقى بالعباس بن عبد المطلب، فقال اللهم إنا كنا نتوسل إليك بنبينا فتسقينا وإنا نتوسل إليك بعم نبينا فاسقنا قال: فيسقون
english_blocks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Ansari related to us. He said: My father, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna, related to me, from Thumamah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Anas, from Anas:

When they suffered drought, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, would seek rain through al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib. He would say, “O Allah, we used to seek a means to You through our Prophet, and You would give us rain. We seek a means to You through the uncle of our Prophet, so give us rain.” He said: They would be given rain.

arabic_blocks: [966] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال عبد الله بن أبي بكر أنه سمع عباد بن تميم يحدث أباه عن عمه عبد الله بن زيد أن النبي ﷺ خرج إلى المصلى فاستسقى فاستقبل القبلة وقلب رداءه وصلى ركعتين قال أبو عبد الله كان ابن عيينة يقول هو صاحب الأذان ولكنه وهم لأن هذا عبد الله بن زيد بن عاصم المازني مازن الأنصار
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr said that he heard ‘Abbad ibn Tamim relating to his father, from his uncle, ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer ground and sought rain. He faced the qibla, turned his cloak and prayed two units.

Abu ‘Abdullah said: Ibn ‘Uyaynah used to say that he was the one associated with the call to prayer, but he was mistaken, because this is ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn ‘Asim al-Mazini, from the Mazin of the Ansar.

arabic_blocks: [967] حدثنا محمد قال: أخبرنا أبو ضمرة أنس بن عياض قال: حدثنا شريك بن عبد الله بن أبي نمر أنه سمع أنس بن مالك يذكر أن رجلا دخل يوم الجمعة من باب كان وجاه المنبر ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبل رسول الله ﷺ قائما، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت المواشي وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يغيثنا قال: فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، فقال اللهم اسقنا اللهم اسقنا اللهم اسقنا قال أنس ولا والله ما نرى في السماء من سحاب ولا قزعة ولا شيئا وما بيننا وبين سلع من بيت ولا دار قال: فطلعت من ورائه سحابة مثل الترس فلما توسطت السماء انتشرت ثم أمطرت قال والله ما رأينا الشمس ستا ثم دخل رجل من ذلك الباب في الجمعة المقبلة ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبله قائما، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت الأموال وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يمسكها قال: فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، ثم قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا اللهم على الآكام والجبال والآجام والظراب والأودية ومنابت الشجر قال: فانقطعت وخرجنا نمشي في الشمس قال شريك فسألت أنسا أهو الرجل الأول قال لا أدري
english_blocks: Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu Damrah Anas ibn ‘Iyad informed us. He said: Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir related to us that he heard Anas ibn Malik mentioning:

A man entered on Friday through a door facing the pulpit while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to send us rain.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands and said, “O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain.”

Anas said: No, by Allah, we could see no cloud in the sky, not even a small patch, nor anything at all. There was no house or dwelling between us and Sal‘. He said: A cloud like a shield rose from behind it. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out and then rained.

He said: By Allah, we did not see the sun for six days. Then a man entered through that door on the following Friday while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, upon the high ground, the mountains, the thickets, the low hills, the valleys and the places where trees grow.” He said: It stopped, and we went out walking in the sunshine.
Sharik said: I asked Anas, “Was he the first man?” He said, “I do not know.”

arabic_blocks: [968] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن شريك عن أنس بن مالك أن رجلا دخل المسجد يوم جمعة من باب كان نحو دار القضاء ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبل رسول الله ﷺ قائما، ثم قال: يا رسول الله هلكت الأموال وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يغثنا فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، ثم قال اللهم أغثنا اللهم أغثنا اللهم أغثنا قال أنس ولا والله ما نرى في السماء من سحاب ولا قزعة وما بيننا وبين سلع من بيت ولا دار قال: فطلعت من ورائه سحابة مثل الترس فلما توسطت السماء انتشرت ثم أمطرت فلا والله ما رأينا الشمس ستا ثم دخل رجل من ذلك الباب في الجمعة يعني الثانية ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبله قائما، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت الأموال وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يمسكها عنا قال: فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، ثم قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا اللهم على الآكام والظراب وبطون الأودية ومنابت الشجر قال: فأقلعت وخرجنا نمشي في الشمس قال شريك سألت أنس بن مالك أهو الرجل الأول، فقال: ما أدري
english_blocks: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Sharik, from Anas ibn Malik:

A man entered the mosque on a Friday through a door towards Dar al-Qada’ while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to send us rain.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, come to our aid. O Allah, come to our aid. O Allah, come to our aid.”

Anas said: No, by Allah, we could see no cloud in the sky, not even a small patch. There was no house or dwelling between us and Sal‘. He said: A cloud like a shield rose from behind it. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out and then rained. No, by Allah, we did not see the sun for six days.

Then a man entered through that door on Friday—meaning the second Friday—while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back from us.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, upon the high ground, the low hills, the valley bottoms and the places where trees grow.” He said: It ceased, and we went out walking in the sunshine.
Sharik said: I asked Anas ibn Malik, “Was he the first man?” He said, “I do not know.”

arabic_blocks: [969] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة عن قتادة عن أنس قال بينما رسول الله ﷺ يخطب يوم الجمعة إذ جاءه رجل، فقال: يا رسول الله قحط المطر فادع الله أن يسقينا فدعا فمطرنا فما كدنا أن نصل إلى منازلنا فما زلنا نمطر إلى الجمعة المقبلة قال: فقام ذلك الرجل أو غيره، فقال: يا رسول الله ادع الله أن يصرفه عنا، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا قال: فلقد رأيت السحاب يتقطع يمينا وشمالا يمطرون ولا يمطر أهل المدينة
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on Friday, a man came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the rain has failed, so supplicate to Allah to give us rain.” He supplicated, and rain fell upon us, so that we could hardly reach our homes. Rain continued to fall upon us until the following Friday. He said: That man, or someone else, stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah to turn it away from us.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” He said: I saw the clouds breaking apart to the right and the left. They received rain, but the people of Medina did not.

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah, from Anas, who said:

A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “The livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off.” He supplicated, and rain fell upon us from Friday to Friday. arabic_blocks: [974] حدثنا محمد بن كثير عن سفيان حدثنا منصور والأعمش عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق قال أتيت بن مسعود، فقال إن قريشا أبطؤوا عن الإسلام فدعا عليهم النبي ﷺ فأخذتهم سنة حتى هلكوا فيها وأكلوا الميتة والعظام فجاءه أبو سفيان، فقال: يا محمد جئت تأمر بصلة الرحم وإن قومك هلكوا فادع الله فقرأ { فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين } ثم عادوا إلى كفرهم فذلك قوله تعالى { يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى } يوم بدر قال أبو عبد الله وزاد أسباط عن منصور فدعا رسول الله ﷺ فسقوا الغيث فأطبقت عليهم سبعا وشكا الناس كثرة المطر قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا فانحدرت السحابة عن رأسه فسقوا الناس حولهم
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from Sufyan: Mansur and al-A‘mash related to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said:

I went to Ibn Mas‘ud, and he said: Quraysh were slow to accept Islam, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicated against them. A year of scarcity overtook them, until they were perishing in it and ate carrion and bones. Abu Sufyan came to him and said, “O Muhammad, you came commanding that ties of kinship be maintained, and your people have perished, so supplicate to Allah.” He recited, “So watch for the day when the sky brings clear smoke.” Then they returned to their disbelief. That is His saying, Most High, “The day We strike the greatest blow”—the day of Badr.
Abu ‘Abdullah said: Asbat added, from Mansur:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicated, and they were given rain. It covered them for seven days, and the people complained of the abundance of rain. He said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” The cloud moved down from above his head, and the people around them were given rain.

arabic_blocks: [975] حدثنا محمد بن أبي بكر حدثنا معتمر عن عبيد الله عن ثابت عن أنس قال: كان النبي ﷺ يخطب يوم جمعة فقام الناس فصاحوا فقالوا يا رسول الله قحط المطر واحمرت الشجر وهلكت البهائم فادع الله أن يسقينا، فقال اللهم اسقنا مرتين وأيم الله ما نرى في السماء قزعة من سحاب فنشأت سحابة وأمطرت ونزل عن المنبر فصلى فلما انصرف لم تزل تمطر إلى الجمعة التي تليها فلما قام النبي ﷺ يخطب صاحوا إليه تهدمت البيوت وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يحبسها عنا فتبسم النبي ﷺ، ثم قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا فكشطت المدينة فجعلت تمطر حولها ولا تمطر بالمدينة قطرة فنظرت إلى المدينة وإنها لفي مثل الإكليل
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr related to us. Mu‘tamir related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Thabit, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on a Friday. The people stood up and cried out, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, the rain has failed, the trees have reddened and the animals have perished, so supplicate to Allah to give us rain.” He said, “O Allah, give us rain,” twice. By Allah, we could see no patch of cloud in the sky. A cloud formed and rained. He came down from the pulpit and prayed. When he had finished, it continued raining until the following Friday.

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to deliver the sermon, they cried out to him, “The houses have collapsed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back from us.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, smiled, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” It cleared away from Medina and began raining around it, while not a drop fell in Medina. I looked at Medina, and it was as though it were within a wreath.
